title: Reduction and derived Nakayama
statement:
The finite quotient coefficient has the perfect resolution
$[\mathcal O_{E,X}\xrightarrow{\pi_E^n}\mathcal O_{E,X}]$, so $K_n$ is the cone of
$\pi_E^n\colon K\to K$. If a derived-complete complex has $K_1=0$, it is zero.
Consequently a morphism between derived-complete complexes is an isomorphism
whenever its first derived reduction is an isomorphism.

steps.text:
The coefficient sequence is exact on the profinite point, hence after pullback,
and it supplies the two-term resolution ([lem-weil-pbc-standard-quotients-perfect],
[det-pe-derived-nakayama-resolution]). The short exact sequences between
successive powers of $\pi_E$ show inductively that $K_1=0$ implies $K_n=0$ for
all $n$, and completeness then gives $K=0$. Derived completeness is closed under
cones, so applying this to the cone proves the last assertion
([det-pe-derived-nakayama-first-reduction]; compare
[lem-weil-pbc-levelwise-isomorphism-cones], where all reductions are assumed to
vanish).
